**Finding: deviation (Section 14.1, ¶p0121) — high severity, assignment.**

- **Issue:** The mutual assignment bar gives us no affiliate carve-out, no reasonableness standard on consent, and — most importantly — its "direct competitor" carve-back lets Commerce One withhold consent to an assignment made in connection with our own merger, acquisition or asset sale.
- **Checked:** Section 11 (Term and Termination) contains no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right, so no edit is needed there.
- **Redline (validated, preferred level):** Commerce One may assign only with our prior written consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to a Corio competitor; Corio may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all related assets. Fallback (mutual notice-based successor right with reasonable consent for other assignments) offered in the comment.
